data.name: Aabdar
data.gender_notes: Aabdar is used as a male descriptive name in Persian and Urdu tradition.
data.short_meaning: Lustrous; bright; polished; possessing water (of a gem or a blade)
data.long_meaning: Aabdar (آبدار) is a Persian name meaning “Lustrous; bright; polished; possessing water”. It is a compound of āb (آب) 'water' and -dār 'having, possessing'. In Persian and Urdu the word describes a polished gem, a watered sword-blade, or fresh lustre generally. The name therefore carries the sense of brilliant, well-tempered brightness.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aabdar carries the meaning Lustrous; bright; polished. Any spiritual reading placed on the name is interpretive and is labelled as such; the lexical meaning is the documented core.
data.etymology: Persian compound āb (آب) 'water' + dār 'having, possessing'; applied to polished gems and watered steel.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aabdar total 18, reducing to 9. Number 9 is associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What does the name Aabdar mean?
faq.a: Aabdar means Lustrous; bright; polished; possessing water.

faq.q: What is the origin of the name Aabdar?
What language does the name Aabdar come from?
faq.a: Aabdar is used in Persian and Urdu.

faq.q: Is Aabdar a boy's name or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aabdar is used as a male descriptive name in Persian and Urdu tradition.

faq.q: How is Aabdar written in Persian and Urdu?
faq.a: Aabdar is written آبدار in both Persian and Urdu, and आबदार in Devanagari.

faq.q: What is the linguistic root of Aabdar?
faq.a: The root of Aabdar is Persian ābdār (آبدار), from āb (آب) water plus -dār, having.

faq.q: What is the etymology of Aabdar?
faq.a: Aabdar is a Persian compound of āb (water) and dār (having, possessing); it was applied to polished gems and watered steel.

faq.q: Does Aabdar appear in the Qur'an?
faq.a: No. Aabdar is of Persian origin and is not a Qur'anic name.

faq.q: What does Aabdar describe in Persian and Urdu?
faq.a: In Persian and Urdu, ābdār describes a polished gem, a watered sword-blade, or fresh lustre generally.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Aabdar verified?
faq.a: Yes. The meaning Lustrous; bright; polished rests on the Persian compound āb water plus dār having, applied to polished gems and watered steel.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Aabdar?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aabdar total 18, reducing to 9. Number 9 is traditionally associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Aabdar?
faq.a: Variants and alternative transliterations include Abdara and Aabdara.

faq.q: Is Aabdar the same as Aabad?
faq.a: No. Aabad (آباد) means inhabited, cultivated; Aabdar (آبدار) means lustrous, polished. They share the Persian element āb (water) but are different words.

faq.q: Where is the name Aabdar used today?
faq.a: Aabdar circulates chiefly in Persian and Urdu naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
